@backend-architect @engineering-frontend-developer

We need to represent the full clinical workflow as a pipeline with metrics 
at each stage. This is the most important view for ops to understand where 
cases are getting stuck.

THE WORKFLOW (in order):
1. Case onboarded (Patient created, CaseRegistered in PatientAuditLog)
2. Assessment assigned (AllocatePatient created, CliniciainUserId set)
3. Assessment in progress (clinician working)
4. Report drafted (result generated, IsResultGenerate = 1)
5. Report approved by manager (check PatientAuditLog for approval event, 
   also check AllocatePatient.Status)
6. Goals set by clinician (PatientSPMAssessmentFNPGoal, 
   PatientReelsAssessmentFnpGoal, PatientISAAssessmentFnpGoal etc)
7. Goals approved by manager (PatientGoalApprovalRequest + 
   PatientGoalApprovalRequestGoal WHERE Status = 'Approved')
8. Assessment closed (AllocatePatient.Status = 'Closed' or similar — 
   check actual Status values in AllocatePatient)

IMPORTANT: Each of steps 4-7 repeats per assessment type. A child with SPM + 
DP3 has two separate report approval flows and two separate goal approval flows.

BACKEND — new endpoint:

GET /api/pipeline
Query params: centreId (optional), dateFrom (optional), dateTo (optional)

First, query DISTINCT Status from AllocatePatient and log all values — 
we need to know the actual status strings before writing the logic.

Returns:
{
  stages: [
    { 
      stage: "Onboarded",
      count: number,
      avgDaysInStage: number
    },
    {
      stage: "Assessment Assigned",
      count: number,
      avgDaysInStage: number,
      stuckCount: number    -- in this stage > 7 days
    },
    {
      stage: "Report Drafted",
      count: number,
      avgDaysInStage: number,
      stuckCount: number
    },
    {
      stage: "Report Pending Approval",
      count: number,
      avgDaysInStage: number,
      stuckCount: number    -- pending approval > 3 days
    },
    {
      stage: "Goals Set",
      count: number,
      avgDaysInStage: number
    },
    {
      stage: "Goals Pending Approval", 
      count: number,
      avgDaysInStage: number,
      stuckCount: number
    },
    {
      stage: "Closed",
      count: number
    }
  ],
  
  managerApprovalStats: {
    reportApprovalRate: number,      -- % of reports approved vs total drafted
    reportAvgApprovalHours: number,
    goalApprovalRate: number,        -- % of goal requests approved
    goalAvgApprovalHours: number,
    byManager: [{
      managerId, firstName, lastName, centreName,
      reportApprovalRate: number,
      reportPending: number,
      goalApprovalRate: number,
      goalPending: number,
      avgApprovalHours: number
    }]
  },
  
  stuckCases: [{    -- cases with no movement in 7+ days
    patientId, patientDisplayId, firstName, lastName,
    centreName, currentStage, daysStuck, clinicianName, managerName
  }]
}

FRONTEND — add Pipeline tab to main dashboard nav (make it the second tab, 
right after Overview — this is the most important operational view):

Section 1 — Pipeline funnel visualisation:
Horizontal funnel chart showing count at each stage. Each stage is a 
trapezoid/bar that narrows as cases drop off. Colour: green for healthy 
stages, amber if stuckCount > 0, red if stuckCount is significant.
Clicking a stage highlights the stuck cases table below.

Section 2 — Manager approval rates (2 metric cards):
- Report Approval Rate: XX% (with avg turnaround Xh)
- Goal Approval Rate: XX% (with avg turnaround Xh)
Both cards are prominent. Red if rate < 70%, amber if < 90%, green if > 90%.

Section 3 — Approval rates by manager table:
Manager | Centre | Report Approval % | Report Pending | Goal Approval % | 
Goal Pending | Avg Turnaround
Sort by worst performance first (lowest approval rate at top) so ops can 
immediately see who needs a nudge.

Section 4 — Stuck cases table:
Cases with no movement in 7+ days. 
Patient ID | Centre | Current Stage | Days Stuck | Clinician | Manager
Red highlight if > 14 days stuck. This is the most urgent section — 
visually make it feel urgent without being aggressive.

This is a modern AI-era dashboard. The pipeline funnel should be visually 
compelling — this is the hero view of the entire product. Use smooth 
gradients on the funnel bars, clean stage labels, clear counts. The approval 
rate cards should be large and readable from across a room. Typography 
should be confident and clear throughout. Microinteractions on hover — 
row highlights, subtle transitions. This should feel like a product the ops 
team actually wants to open every morning, not a spreadsheet.
